title: Choose Gapl's new visual world
question: A fresh world for Gapl: premium, calm on a phone, no costume. Keep the roll, take my pick, take the category standard, or re-roll.

options.label: The Shortlist
options.lineage: Training & Placement cell circulars: Ref. No., Sub:, the numbered shortlist
options.thesis: Every placement season ends in one circular, the shortlist; Gapl tells you whether your name makes it and what puts it there.
materials: crisp A4 sheets on one bottle-green ground
document serif for the subject line, sharp grotesk for UI, tabular figures
options.viewport: The page is the circular: a Ref/date line, the subject line at display scale ('Sub: Why your name isn't on the shortlist.'), the role/tier enquiry written as a fill-in sentence with the action inside it, then the shortlist with your row blank.
options.risk: Read as another office-document costume if the letterhead details outweigh the typography; it has to be set like a premium editorial page, not a sarkari form.

raised.raise: Statuses are typed into the circular as words (Shortlisted, Not shortlisted: 3 gaps), never badges or pills.
Row state is a mark (tick, dash, strike-through); colour only repeats it.
Every section is headed by its literal document field: Sub, Ref, Remarks, Enclosure.
One ground colour owns the whole site; paper sheets are the only other material.
Every report has a face (verdict and reason) and a back (the numbers), never mixed.
One element per viewport is cut biggest: the subject line on landing, the verdict on the report.

options.label: The Recruiter's Read
options.lineage: a resume after a recruiter's six seconds: highlighter, red pen, margin note
options.thesis: Your resume, read the way a recruiter reads it: what they saw, what they skipped, and the one line that sank it.
materials: one large white A4 resume page on a charcoal desk
highlighter strokes and red-pen marks as the only ornament
options.viewport: A full-height sample resume page with the recruiter's marks on it, the verdict written in the margin, the headline over the desk and a drop zone that swaps the sample for your own page.
options.risk: The most familiar card here: annotated-resume heroes are common in resume tools, and hand marks turn kitsch if they are drawn rather than precise.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The report as a live transcript typed onto glass.
options.viewport: An 80-column transcript printing the verdict line by line.
options.risk: Dark-neon is the AI default and a costume of the tool.
options.case: Loses both axes: students don't see themselves in a machine room, and an all-mono transcript hides the report's structure.
options.kept: States print themselves as words rather than chrome.

options.label: Normalled Jackfield
options.thesis: Every gap as a broken link line on black glass.
options.viewport: Numbered lanes, each skill tied or broken.
options.risk: Unreadable to anyone who hasn't worked a studio.
options.case: Loses both axes: foreign to the audience, and a lane grid fights a phone-first report.
options.kept: State is drawn by mark, never by colour alone.

options.label: Industrial Quote Grammar
options.thesis: "REJECT" in straight quotes, hazard stripes under every gap.
options.viewport: Giant quoted caps naming the verdict over a striped gap.
options.risk: Gimmicky, the exact thing you asked to leave behind.
options.case: Holds some audience pull with Gen Z but loses on clarity and on your no-gimmick brief.
options.kept: Every zone is labelled with its literal name; wayfinding is reading.

options.label: Indoor Weather Sun
options.thesis: One hall, one sun, your silhouette in the mirror.
options.viewport: A vast amber band with the verdict on the horizon.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link to placements, and duotone haze buries data.
options.kept: Total colour commitment: one ground owns everything.

options.label: Wax Pack Card
options.lineage: trading cards: face and stat back
options.thesis: Your resume as a player card you flip for the stats.
options.viewport: A dealt card with your verdict on the face.
options.risk: Gamified, which the brand rules out.
options.case: Loses both axes: baseball cards aren't this audience's world and collecting reads as a game.
options.kept: Face and back: the verdict on the front, the numbers behind it.

options.label: Punk Paste-up
options.viewport: A crooked flyer shouting the verdict.
options.risk: Chaotic and unpremium, against the whole brief.
options.case: Loses both axes: noisy on a phone and nobody trusts a zine with their career.
options.kept: Hierarchy is brutal: one thing per view is cut biggest.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean, light product page, the way Linear or Stripe would ship a resume tool.
materials: the real report as product UI
canonCard.viewport: Centred headline, an upload box, and the sample report as a crisp product screenshot below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Jobscan, Teal and every AI resume tool by design.
